title: DNA and Protein Synthesis
seo_title: Anatomy and Physiology 12: DNA and Protein Synthesis Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Gene expression, through protein synthesis, is an interaction between genes and the environment: DNA structure and replication, transcription and translation, the genetic code, and mutations and gene regulation. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Anatomy and Physiology 12)
meta_desc: Free Anatomy and Physiology 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): DNA replication, transcription and translation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Each codon of three bases codes for one amino acid.
body_html:
How to think about it

DNA is a double helix of nucleotides; A pairs with T and C with G. In replication, the strands separate and DNA polymerase builds new complementary strands (semi-conservative replication).

In transcription, RNA polymerase copies a gene into mRNA in the nucleus (U replaces T). In translation at the ribosome, tRNA reads the mRNA codons and brings amino acids to build a protein. Mutations change the DNA sequence and can change the protein.

Example

What is the mRNA made from the DNA strand TAC?

T→A, A→U, C→G

Answer: AUG

Example

Where does translation happen?

Protein factories

Answer: at the ribosome

Common mistakes

  • Writing T instead of U in mRNA.
  • Mixing up transcription and translation.
  • Thinking every mutation changes the protein.

items.q: What does semi-conservative replication mean?
c: both strands of the new molecule are new
each new DNA molecule has one original strand and one new strand
items.e: Shown by the Meselson–Stahl experiment.

items.q: What are introns?
c: non-coding sections of a gene that are removed from pre-mRNA
the coding sections that stay in mRNA
items.e: The exons are joined in splicing.

One base changes: AUG UUU AAA becomes AUG UUU GAA. What happens to the protein?
c: The protein gets one amino acid longer.
One amino acid changes: Lys becomes Glu.
Every amino acid after the change is different.
items.e: A substitution changes only one codon: AAA → GAA.

items.q: How does decreased acetylation of histones affect a gene?
c: the chromatin becomes more condensed, so transcription is inhibited
items.e: Acetylation loosens chromatin.
